az_dominatrix_crack_boulder.blurb: A large boulder beside the Cochise Trail in the East Stronghold bouldering zone of Cochise Stronghold. Eight lines are recorded here: seven boulder problems running from very easy slab and crack lines through the middle V grades to a couple of hard ones, plus one steep crack that is also climbed on gear or a top rope at the low 5.12 level. The crack on the boulder's southeast corner is the main draw, and it is tall enough that a rope or a stack of pads and spotters makes sense. It is a quick stop on the way to the bigger boulder cluster further along the trail.
az_dominatrix_crack_boulder.parking_note: Leave the car at the campground lot at the end of Ironwood Road, in the East Stronghold, then walk from the campground.
az_dominatrix_crack_boulder.approach: From the campground head southeast to the Nature Loop Trail, follow it about an eighth of a mile to the Cochise Trail, cross the usually dry wash, and continue roughly a third of a mile. The boulder sits right beside the trail.

az_north_mesa.blurb: North Mesa is a formation in the Cathedral Rock complex of mesas and towers west of Highway 179 near Sedona. All eight routes here are trad, with most in the 5.10 range and a few at 5.11, and at least one of them runs to four pitches. Walls face nearly every direction, so you can usually chase sun or shade depending on the day. It is the first formation you meet on the right when hiking the standard approach to the neighbouring tower, which makes it a handy pairing for a day in the area, though expect a sustained, moderate-and-up grade range with no easy warm-ups.
az_north_mesa.parking_note: Park at the trailhead near the end of Back O' Beyond Road, which turns west off Highway 179; it is the same lot used for The Mace.

az_mace_the.blurb: A freestanding tower in the Cathedral Rock complex just west of Highway 179 at Sedona, and probably the most famous and most climbed formation in the area. Seven of its eight routes are trad and one is a top-rope, spanning roughly 5.9 to 5.11, with the standard line stretching to five pitches. Expect company on busy days. Because the tower stands alone, it is a long multi-pitch outing rather than a quick crag session, and the approach adds a short scrambly section on the way up.
az_mace_the.parking_note: Park at the trailhead near the end of Back O' Beyond Road, reached by turning west off Highway 179.
az_mace_the.approach: Follow the cairned trail toward the east side of the formation, through a short third-class section, then traverse across to the base of the tower.

az_lost_elden.blurb: A small, quiet cirque on Mt. Elden above Flagstaff, sitting just north of an old bouldering hideaway. Its rock is dacite, the rough, high-friction volcanic stone typical of the Elden crags. Of the eight climbs, all are trad, ranging from an easy scramble up through moderate lines to a few in the 5.10s and 5.11s and one at 5.12. Mostly single pitches. Few climbers come here, and the routes are scattered around the cirque rather than grouped on one wall, so expect to wander. The approach goes up steep slabs with plenty of cactus and yucca.

az_middle_section_2.blurb: A stretch of canyon walls in West Clear Creek, with cliffs of 200 to 300 feet rising right from the water's edge. This is sandstone with plenty of cracks, and the climbing is mostly traditional, with a single sport route among the eight. The grade range starts at 5.10 and tops out at 5.12, with about half the routes at 5.10 and the rest split between 5.11 and 5.12, so it suits strong leaders rather than beginners. Fixed protection is sparse, and the ground-up style of the canyon means you should bring a full rack.

az_sphinx_aka_cibola_mitten.blurb: A rounded dome of roughly 400 feet near West Sedona, with a smaller tower at each of its east and west ends, tucked among the formations of the Coffeepot Rock area. Climbing here is almost all trad: eight routes, mostly in the 5.10 range with a couple at 5.11, though one or two are marked as sport or top-rope. It sits between the Jordan Road and Soldier Pass trailheads, and the hike in heads for the Cibola Pass trail. The area is little visited, so you are likely to have the place largely to yourself.
